title: Donut Binary — Secondary Segment Color

complexity.rationale: The 2-segment (isBoolean) donut already exists and mostly works - this corrects one specific, well-documented gap against the donut-binary skill, at a single coordinated site: forcing the secondary segment's fill to secondary-gray (adapting the same test-expression color-swap pattern already speced for donut-emphasize/Line's primarySeries). Revised down from an earlier draft that also proposed changing SegmentLabel's isBoolean early-return - on review, the donut-binary skill's 'Only the primary segment is labeled' bullet refers to the center-hole DonutSummary value (which already correctly shows only the primary segment's value via getBooleanDonutSummaryGroupMark/getSummaryValueText), not the outside-the-ring SegmentLabel component. SegmentLabel remains intentionally fully suppressed for isBoolean donuts, unchanged. No open design questions remain on the one gap left in scope.

summary: The existing isBoolean (2-segment binary) donut variant has one gap against the documented donut-binary design: the secondary/complementary segment's arc always renders via the normal categorical color scale - it's never forced to chart.donut.color.secondary-gray as the design requires, confirmed by getArcMark (donutUtils.ts:48-76) having no isBoolean handling at all. The center-hole DonutSummary value already correctly shows only the primary segment's value for binary donuts (getBooleanDonutSummaryGroupMark/getSummaryValueText's isBoolean branch), which satisfies the skill's 'Only the primary segment is labeled' requirement - SegmentLabel (the outside-the-ring direct label) is a separate, unrelated component and stays fully suppressed for isBoolean donuts as it is today, not a gap. packages/vega-spec-builder (s1) has the identical arc-fill gap, but per project direction this work is s2-only - s1 is intentionally left unchanged.
requirements: When isBoolean is true, the secondary (non-primary) segment's arc fill must always be chart.donut.color.secondary-gray (#C6C6C6/gray-400), overriding the normal categorical color-scale rule - regardless of what color the data's second row would otherwise map to via the color domain.
When isBoolean is true, the primary segment continues to render its own normal categorical color, unaffected.

The primary segment is the first data point, consistent with isBoolean's existing documented convention ('displays the first datapoint as a percent') - the secondary segment is the complementary/remaining share.

SegmentLabel (direct labels) remains fully suppressed for isBoolean donuts - already correct today (`if (isBoolean) return [];` in getSegmentLabelMarks); no change needed here. The skill's 'Only the primary segment is labeled' intent is already satisfied by the center-hole DonutSummary value.
No separate swatch legend for binary donuts - already correct today (DonutSummary in the center hole already serves this role); no change needed here.

designTokens.usage: Fixed fill for the secondary/complementary segment of a binary donut, regardless of the data's own color-domain mapping.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Per donut-benchmark, the primary segment's color can already switch to a sentiment color when Benchmark+Semantic is set - confirm the secondary segment still renders secondary-gray in that combination, unaffected by the primary segment's sentiment override.

Emphasize's gray-swap and binary's forced secondary-gray could look redundant/conflicting on a 2-segment donut - confirm expected behavior when both are configured together (same open concern already flagged in donut-emphasize's edge cases).

edgeCases.case: User-supplied custom color scale/domain where the secondary row has its own explicit categorical color
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The secondary-gray override must always win for isBoolean donuts, regardless of what the color domain would otherwise assign to that row.

SegmentLabel continues to render nothing at all for isBoolean donuts, unchanged from today - this is intentional, not a suppressed-in-error gap; the primary segment's value is already surfaced via the center-hole DonutSummary.

The arc-fill gap is confirmed identical in packages/vega-spec-builder (s1) - its donutUtils.ts has no isBoolean handling in its arc fill either - but per project direction this work is s2-only; s1 is intentionally left unchanged, not a gap to track here.

crossCutting.notes: requiresNewSignalOrScale is false - this is a new production rule on the existing arc fill encode (a static isBoolean/primary-row test expression, no new signal or scale). requiresS1S2Parity is false: per project direction, this work is scoped to s2 only. packages/vega-spec-builder (s1) has the identical gap (no isBoolean handling in getArcMark), but s1 is intentionally left unchanged, not treated as a parity gap.

implementationPlan.change: In getArcMark, add isBoolean and idKey to the destructured options and extend the fill encode with a test expression: when isBoolean and the row is not the primary (first) data point, use secondary-gray; otherwise use the existing getColorProductionRule(color, colorScheme) result. Identify the primary row by comparing datum[idKey] against the existing `${name}_booleanData` derived data source's single row.
Add tests for the secondary-gray override on the arc fill encode.

New story (in the non-pre-alpha Donut story location used for new s2 donut feature work going forward) exercising isBoolean, confirming the primary segment shows its category color and the secondary segment renders secondary-gray.
